original_question: Let pi: St(V, R) -> PE(V) be the homomorphism from Theorem 2.11(a), and assume the root system R is irreducible of finite rank. Find sufficient conditions under which the kernel Ker(pi) is central.
target_in_paper: Theorem 1.3 (the finite-rank case), read together with Conjecture 1.1 and Proposition 1.2 in the introduction.
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the canonical homomorphism pi from the Steinberg group to the projective elementary group, focuses on the centrality of Ker(pi), and restricts attention to the irreducible finite-rank case, which is exactly the part of the paper where the main finite-rank centrality result is discussed.
missing_details: The paper is about a Jordan pair V, not just an abstract group-theoretic pair of symbols St(V,R) and PE(V).

The relevant grading data are not merely a root system R, but a 3-graded root system (R,R_1) together with a root grading ℜ of V; the Steinberg group is written with this grading datum, not just with R alone.

The paper's centrality problem is stated under stronger structural hypotheses on the grading (the introduction and the main theorem use the paper's idempotent/fully idempotent root-grading framework, not an arbitrary root grading).
The exact finite-rank sufficient condition proved in the paper is missing: the theorem isolates a rank threshold, rather than asking for unspecified sufficient conditions.
The intended conclusion is that Ker(pi) is central in St(V,ℜ), i.e. Ker(pi) is contained in the center of the Steinberg group, not merely abelian or normal.
The nearby context in Proposition 1.2 links this centrality statement to a universal-central-extension formulation; the draft omits that paper-explicit reformulation.
refined_question: Let V be a Jordan pair with the paper's root-grading hypotheses (in particular, a fully idempotent root grading ℜ by a 3-graded root system (R,R_1)), and let pi: St(V,ℜ) -> PE(V) be the canonical homomorphism of Theorem 2.11(a). Assume that R is irreducible of finite rank and that rank(R) >= 5. Is Ker(pi) contained in the center of St(V,ℜ)?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, in the setting of Proposition 1.2, under the same hypotheses one may ask whether pi: St(V,ℜ) -> PE(V) is the universal central extension of PE(V).
justification: The draft is clearly aimed at the paper's centrality problem for the canonical map pi, but it is looser than the paper in two ways: it suppresses the Jordan-pair/root-grading setup and it asks for unspecified sufficient conditions instead of isolating the exact sufficient condition singled out in the introduction. The introduction first formulates the general centrality question as Conjecture 1.1, then gives the universal-central-extension reformulation in Proposition 1.2, and finally states the proved finite-rank case in Theorem 1.3. So the sharp paper-faithful refinement is the finite-rank statement from Theorem 1.3, with the notation restored from Theorem 2.11(a).
